label: lf-verify-lean
topic: Independent re-check of lf-lean-fire.json and FireCoatingCertificate.lean: are the heat formulas right, and does each theorem say what its docstring claims?
summary:
The formulas are the standard ones, but three of the elimination theorems are unsafe as physical certificates. The two ignition eliminations use no-loss ignition times, which are lower bounds on the real ignition time, so "formula time < treq" does not show the material ignites before treq. The finite-time elimination has no hypothesis linking the one-node curve to the real back face, although its docstring says it does. I did not run Lean (7-minute budget), so this is a read of the statements, not a re-check of the proofs. I wrote no files and changed nothing in the repo; the fixes are listed as recommendations.

Sources: I opened one page (Wikipedia, Lumped-element model), which confirms series resistance, the lumped transient and its time constant. The thick-ignition formula and the penetration depth are not confirmed from an opened text: the SFPE guide page and a UCL paper both returned HTTP 403.

Verdict per claim:
- CONFIRMED: series resistance R = d/k + Rs + Ra and the steady back-face rise algebra (backRise_le_ΔT, backRise_antitone_thickness, backRise_lower, steady_eliminates, char_lowers_rise, char_eliminates). Caveat: there is no fire-side film resistance, so ΔT must be the coating-surface temperature minus ambient; using gas temperature overstates the rise.
- CONFIRMED: lumped transient Tss(1 - exp(-t/τ)) with τ = C/h, and relax_ode. The Biot-number validity condition (< 0.1) appears nowhere in the file.
- CONFIRMED (algebra only): thick_iff_time matches its docstring exactly. The sqrt(αt) depth itself was not found in an opened source.
- CONFIRMED: thin solid with loss (thinTemp, thin_never_ignites, critical flux h(Tig - T0)).
- WEAKER: thin_reaches_Tig shows the temperature equals Tig at t*, but not that t* is positive or the first such time.
- UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: tigThick = (π/4)·kρc·ΔT²/q². It agrees with the semi-infinite constant-flux solution as I recall it, but I opened no text containing it.
- WEAKER and UNSAFE: thick_ignition_eliminates and thin_ignition_eliminates. Docstring: "prove ignition happens before the required non-ignition time". Statement: only that the no-loss formula value is below treq. Inside the file's own lossy thin model, t* = -(C/h)·ln(1 - x) ≥ C·ΔT/q, so real ignition is later than tigThin. Neither theorem requires the thick or thin regime (no link to thick_iff_time), and ΔTig ≥ 0 is not required in the thick one.
- DIFFERENT: transient_eliminates. Docstring calls the one-node response a "hypothesis, not axiom"; in fact the conclusion is about relax(backRise…) itself. A one-node curve starts rising at once, while a real slab's back face lags, so the bound can overstate early-time rise.
- OVERSTATED: worked_example docstring says "eliminated before any test", but it is steady-state only, which section 1 itself says proves nothing at a finite test time. The arithmetic is right (447.6 K bound, 490.8 K actual).
- CONFIRMED: peak_ge_mean and hrr_eliminates match their docstrings; hχ, hm, hH are unused.
- MINOR (JSON): it says "16 theorems"; the file has 19, with 16 #print axioms lines. Its finding 4 says "passed check.sh" for physics that check.sh cannot test. The section 5 title mentions critical flux, but no critical flux appears in that section.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: series thermal resistance. Slab resistance is L/(kA), film resistance 1/(hA), and layers in series add; totalR = d/k + Rs + Ra is the per-unit-area form.
findings.evidence_quote: the equivalent resistance is the sum of the resistances of the components
findings.confidence: high. Caveat: the model has no fire-side film resistance, so ΔT must be coating-surface minus ambient; if gas temperature is used the rise is overstated and an elimination is not conservative.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: lumped transient. The first-order solution is exponential with time constant C/(hA); relax and thinTemp (τ = C/h per unit area) match, and relax_ode states the ODE identity for every t.
findings.confidence: high for the formula. The file never states the validity condition; the same page says the Biot number must generally be less than 0.1.

findings.claim: DIFFERENT from docstring: transient_eliminates. The docstring says the one-node response is a 'hypothesis, not axiom', but no hypothesis ties any physical temperature to relax; the conclusion is literally about relax (backRise ...) τ t.
findings.value: conclusion: limit < relax (backRise ΔT d k Rs Ra) τ t
findings.evidence_quote: Model assumption (hypothesis, not axiom): the back-face rise follows the one-node response
findings.confidence: high for the statement mismatch. Medium for the physical concern (a one-node curve rises immediately while a slab's back face lags, so the bound can overstate early rise); that is my own reasoning, with no source opened.

findings.claim: WEAKER and physically UNSAFE: thin_ignition_eliminates and thick_ignition_eliminates. They prove only that the no-loss formula value is below treq, not that ignition happens before treq. In the file's own lossy thin model t* = -(C/h) ln(1-x) with x = h(Tig-T0)/q, and -ln(1-x) >= x gives t* >= C(Tig-T0)/q = tigThin, so real ignition is later than the formula.
findings.value: tigThin is a lower bound on the lossy ignition time; the eliminations need the opposite direction
findings.evidence_quote: enough to prove ignition happens before the required non-ignition time
findings.confidence: high for the thin case (algebra from the file's own definitions). Medium for the thick case (same direction expected by standard reasoning, not derived or sourced here).

findings.claim: UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: thick ignition time t = (π/4)·kρc·(Tig-T0)²/q². It matches the semi-infinite constant-flux surface solution Ts-T0 = 2q·sqrt(t/(π kρc)) as I recall it, but I opened no text containing the formula.
findings.source: https://www.globalspec.com/reference/76862/203279/thermally-thick (HTTP 403, NOT opened); web-search result summary only
findings.confidence: medium: from memory plus a search summary saying the thick exponent on flux is 2 and the thin is 1. The original report's own 'medium' was fair.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED (algebra only): thick_iff_time states exactly what its docstring says, pdepth c α t <= d iff t <= d²/(c²α), for any c > 0.
findings.confidence: high for statement vs docstring. The sqrt(αt) depth was not found in an opened source (Wikipedia Thermal diffusivity and Thermal effusivity do not state it cleanly). The thick/thin test is never used as a hypothesis by the ignition theorems.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: thin solid with loss. Critical flux h(Tig-T0) and thin_never_ignites match their docstrings. WEAKER: thin_reaches_Tig shows the temperature equals Tig at t* but does not prove t* > 0 or that it is the first crossing (both true, just unstated).
findings.confidence: high. The linear loss h(T-T0) is a linearisation; real surface loss includes radiation.

findings.claim: OVERSTATED docstring: worked_example says the candidate is 'eliminated before any test', but it applies steady_eliminates only, which the file itself says proves nothing at a finite test time. The arithmetic is right.
findings.evidence_quote: Says nothing about a finite test time: see section 5.
findings.confidence: high. That pointer is also wrong: the finite-time material is in section 4, not section 5.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: steady and char theorems (backRise_le_ΔT, backRise_antitone_thickness, backRise_lower, steady_eliminates, char_lowers_rise, char_eliminates) and the energy theorems (peak_ge_mean, hrr_eliminates) state what their docstrings say.
findings.value: hχ, hm, hH unused in hrr_eliminates; ht, hC unused in thin_never_ignites
findings.evidence_quote: A char layer (thickness `xc ≥ 0`, conductivity `kc > 0`) can only lower the steady rise.
findings.confidence: high by reading; Lean was not re-run. Keeping the full virgin thickness d plus the char overstates resistance, which is the safe direction for elimination.

findings.claim: MINOR, JSON vs file: the report says '16 theorems', but the file has 19 theorem declarations and 16 #print axioms lines (totalR_pos, backRise_lower, relax_lower are not printed, though they are dependencies of printed ones). Section 5's title mentions critical flux but no critical flux appears there. The report's Wikipedia Thermal_resistance quote was not re-opened by me.

key_claims: The formulas for series resistance, lumped transient, thin solid with loss and critical flux are stated correctly; one opened source supports the first two.

thin_ignition_eliminates and thick_ignition_eliminates point the wrong way for a physical elimination: no-loss ignition times are lower bounds on the real ignition time (shown for the thin case from the file's own lossy model).
transient_eliminates has no hypothesis linking a real temperature to the one-node curve, although its docstring says it does.
The worked-example docstring overstates: it is a steady-state result, not an elimination 'before any test'.
The thick-ignition formula and the penetration depth are not confirmed from an opened text; Lean was not re-run.
recommendations: Restate the ignition eliminations with a model that includes loss: the thin case can use thinTemp and thin_reaches_Tig directly; for the thick case add an explicit hypothesis that losses are negligible, or use net flux q - q_cr.
Add the regime as a hypothesis: thick_ignition_eliminates should require pdepth <= d at the ignition time, thin_ignition_eliminates the opposite or a Biot-number bound.

Rewrite transient_eliminates to take a real temperature function Tb with hypothesis Tb t >= relax (...) τ t, so the model assumption is visibly a hypothesis; or change the docstring to say the theorem is about the model curve only.
Add a fire-side film resistance to totalR, or state in the docstring that ΔT is coating-surface temperature minus ambient.
Change the worked_example docstring to 'steady-state rise exceeds the limit', drop 'eliminated before any test', and fix the 'see section 5' pointer to section 4.
Add the two small lemmas missing from thin_reaches_Tig: t* > 0, and thinTemp < Tig for t < t*.
Correct the JSON count to 19 theorems (16 axiom checks) and keep the thick-ignition formula marked unverified until a text is opened (Quintiere 2006 ch. 7 or the SFPE guide, via library access).
lay_summary: Another agent wrote maths rules about how heat moves through a painted board and had a computer check the maths.
I checked whether those rules match the physics pages I could open, and whether each rule really says what its label says.
The basic heat rules are right.
But two rules about when something catches fire ignore heat escaping, so they say fire starts sooner than it really would, which makes them unsafe for ruling out a paint.
One rule about how fast the back of the board warms up is labelled as resting on an assumption that is not actually written into it.

glossary.thermal resistance: how strongly a layer holds back heat flow; thickness divided by conductivity
glossary.series resistance: layers stacked one after another, whose resistances add up
glossary.film resistance: the resistance of the thin air layer at a surface, equal to 1/h
glossary.back-face rise: how much hotter the unheated side of the board gets than the room
glossary.steady state: the final condition after temperatures stop changing
glossary.lumped (one-node) model: treating a whole object as one temperature with a single time constant
glossary.time constant: the time for a warming object to cover about 63% of the way to its final temperature
glossary.Biot number: a ratio that says whether an object is uniform enough inside for the lumped model to hold
glossary.penetration depth: how far into a solid a heating pulse has reached, growing like the square root of time
glossary.thermal diffusivity: how fast temperature changes spread through a material (α)
glossary.thermally thick: the heat pulse has not yet reached the back of the layer
glossary.thermally thin: the layer is so thin that it has nearly one temperature throughout
glossary.thermal inertia: the product kρc; high values mean the surface heats slowly
glossary.heat flux: heating power per unit area hitting the surface
glossary.critical flux: the heating level below which the surface never gets hot enough to ignite
glossary.ignition time: how long heating takes for the surface to reach its ignition temperature
glossary.lower bound: a value the true answer cannot be below
glossary.elimination certificate: a proof that a candidate must fail a stated limit under stated assumptions
glossary.docstring: the plain-language comment written above a theorem
glossary.hypothesis: an assumption written into a theorem that must hold for it to apply
glossary.HRR: heat release rate, the power a burning material gives off
glossary.char: the burnt carbon layer that forms on a heated coating and insulates it
